This lab is due Friday (9/18) by 11:59pm on Gradescope. Note: Labs will typically be due the following Wednesday. This deadline is extended to handle any GitHub issues you may run into.

::: {.callout-note}
Note: Part of your grade it to make commits and push them up to your repo at the appropriate times. I want you to build good habits! Please do not ignore these instructions as you move through the lab.
:::

Setup-1. Create a new GitHub repo on GitHub. Name the Repo *Lab-3*. Note: Make sure to add a README file when creating your GitHub repo. 

Setup-2. Clone this repo to your computer. 

1. Create a `.qmd` file and save your file (named something appropriate). Create a level-2 section header called *Question-1*. Click pull in the Git tab. Report the message Git gives you, and explain why this makes sense.

::: {.callout-note}
Render your document, commit, and push all of your changes up to GitHub. Be sure to have a useful commit message.
:::

2. Should `install.packages()` go in your .qmd file, or should this be typed in your Console. Explain your response. 

3. Should `library()` go in your .qmd file, or should this be typed in your Console. Explain your response

::: {.callout-note}
Render your document, commit, and push all of your changes up to GitHub. Be sure to have a useful commit message.
:::

4. See the following code below. 

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
palmerpenguins::penguins
```

This could should not work. Explain why not.

5. To fix question 4's code block, your friend suggests running `install.packages("palmerpenguins")`. Your other friend suggests `install.packages("palmerpenguins")` and `library(palmerpenguins)`. Who is right? Explain your response. 

::: {.callout-note}
Render your document, commit, and push all of your changes up to GitHub. Be sure to have a useful commit message.
:::

6. library the `dplyr` package. Render your document. Do you notice the warning message that is given? Use the correct code chunk argument to hide this warning message.

7. Pull up the help file for `dplyr` and visit the first "Useful links" url. Click on the `arrange()` function to pull up the documentation. Next, arrange the `iris` data set by `Petal.Length`. Save this as `iris2`. Run `head()` on `iris2` and print the results, showing you arranged the data set correctly. 

8. Go to your repo on GitHub. Click on the the clock underneath the Code bar that you used to clone your GitHub repo. Take a screenshot (you can use a snipping tool, or screenshot the entire page) of your commits. Save this in an images folder in your GitHub repo. Then, embed this picture into your .qmd file. 

Congrats! Render for one file time, make one final commit (doesn't need to be in your picture) and upload your PDF to Gradescope.
